verses.1: Then, what is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
verses.2: Much in every way. First of all, that the words of God were entrusted to them.
verses.3: But what if some did not believe? Will their unbelief nullify the faithfulness of God?
verses.4: By no means! Let God be proved true, and every human a liar, just as it is written: "That you might be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged."
verses.5: But if our wrongdoing somehow brings about the righteousness of God, what should we say? Is God unjust in bringing about wrath? I am speaking as a human.
verses.6: By no means! Otherwise, how would God judge the world?
verses.7: If indeed the truth of God were to be magnified through my lie for his glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
verses.8: And why, as we are slandered and as some suppose we say, "Let us do evil that good may come from it," whose judgment is just.
verses.9: Then what? Are we better off? Not at all. For we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin,
verses.10: just as it is written: "There is no one righteous, not even one,
verses.11: there is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
verses.12: All have turned aside, together they have become useless; there is no one who does good, not even one.
verses.13: Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit; the poison of vipers is on their lips,
verses.14: their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness;
verses.15: their feet are swift to shed blood;
verses.16: ruin and anguish are in their paths,
verses.17: and they do not know the way of peace.
verses.18: There is no fear of God before their eyes."
verses.19: Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
verses.20: For through the works of the law, no flesh will be justified before him, since through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
verses.21: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, attested by the law and the prophets—
verses.22: the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, for all who believe, for there is no distinction.
verses.23: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
verses.24: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.25: whom God put forward as a sacrifice of atonement through faith in his blood, to demonstrate his righteousness, because of the passing over of the sins previously committed,
verses.26: in his forbearance, to demonstrate at the present time his righteousness, so that he might be just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus.
verses.27: Then where is boasting? It is excluded. By what law? Of works? No, but by the law of faith.
verses.28: For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.
verses.29: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not also of Gentiles? Yes, of Gentiles also,
verses.30: since indeed there is one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
verses.31: Then does the law nullify faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law.

notes:
Notes
- v. 22: "the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ" — the Greek phrase δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ is a key theological term, often translated as "the righteousness of God" and understood in context as God’s way of justifying people through faith.
- v. 25: "sacrifice of atonement" — the Greek term ἱλαστήριον is theologically significant and often translated as "propitiation" or "atonement." The term refers to the means by which God deals with sin and restores relationship.
- v. 31: "uphold the law" — the Greek term ἱστάνομεν is used to emphasize the continued validity and importance of the law in the context of justification by faith.
